topic: Two-coverage minimax frontier for reverse-KL-regularized offline linear contextual-bandit policy learning: over exact shells indexed jointly by pointwise policy coverage C = ess sup(pi*/pi_ref) and feature-space generalized-eigenvalue coverage D, characterize the minimax sample complexity N*(epsilon;d,C,D,eta) and prove the hard same-shell lower bound Omega~(d D min{eta/epsilon,epsilon^-2}) matching a computable localized-pessimistic linear-reward/Gibbs-policy upper bound; thereby determine when pointwise C beyond feature coverage D is statistically irrelevant, extending Zhao et al. (arXiv:2502.06051/ICLR 2026) and Ji et al. (arXiv:2605.02141), whose closure is tabular-only

open_problems.open_problem: Over exact shells of d-dimensional linear reverse-KL contextual-bandit instances with pointwise coverage C and feature generalized-eigenvalue coverage D, what is the minimax sample complexity across all eta/epsilon regimes, and is it independent of C once D is fixed?

source_refs.claim: The linear/general-function upper bound scales with D2-type single-policy coverage, while the lower bound scales with pointwise C; the paper states that these two quantities cannot generally bound each other.
source_refs.author: Qingyue Zhao, Kaixuan Ji, Heyang Zhao, Tong Zhang, Quanquan Gu

source_refs.claim: The paper closes the fast/slow regularization regimes only for multi-armed bandits and explicitly names extension to linear or general function approximation as future work.
source_refs.author: Kaixuan Ji, Qiwei Di, Heyang Zhao, Qingyue Zhao, Quanquan Gu

open_problems.why_unsolved: Zhao et al. prove a fast-rate upper bound through a function-class D2 coverage quantity but a lower bound through the density-ratio coefficient C, and explicitly note that the two are incomparable up to constants. Ji et al. recover the full min{eta/epsilon, epsilon^-2} phase transition after tabular specialization, where coordinate-wise features can collapse or inflate the distinction between coverage notions, but their closure does not extend to linear function approximation. Shared features therefore obstruct the tabular reduction and leave open which coefficient governs risk on a joint exact shell.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A matching pair of high-probability upper and minimax lower bounds over every nonempty exact (d,C,D,eta) shell, yielding an explicit phase diagram such as N* = Theta-tilde(d D min{eta/epsilon, epsilon^-2}) and a precise statement of when C drops out.

writing_exemplar.why: Its introduction frames an exact sample-complexity question, separates regularization regimes, and closes each with matching upper and lower bounds before explicitly pointing to linear structure as the next gap.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: reverse-KL curvature permits a fast rate -> weak regularization restores the ordinary slow rate -> tabular analysis locates the phase transition -> determine the same transition under linear feature sharing and two distinct coverage notions

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over least-squares reward estimation, a pessimistic bonus, and the Gibbs policy map; adapt the proof that couples one-sided reward error with reverse-KL curvature through a monotonicity/covariance argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already gives the D-based fast-rate upper-bound machinery for the exact reverse-KL objective, so a localized linear analysis can target the proposed shell rate directly.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its separate fast- and slow-regime hard families, change of measure, and pairing-and-counting argument for the multiple-optima slow regime.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its two-regime construction produces exactly the min{eta/epsilon, epsilon^-2} transition that must be lifted from tabular coordinates to shared linear features.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer linear least-squares confidence geometry and pessimistic policy optimization together with norm-matched minimax lower bounds over constrained linear-bandit classes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a computable linear-feature pessimism template and matching minimax geometry absent from the tabular reverse-KL closure.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the exact feasible region and dominance relation between pointwise coverage C and linear feature coverage D under the Gibbs constraint pi*(a|x) proportional to pi_ref(a|x) exp(eta phi(x,a)'theta), and for which feasible pairs can C vary without changing minimax risk at fixed D?

source_refs.claim: Remark 2.8 states that pointwise C and D2-type single-policy coverage cannot generally be bounded by each other up to constant factors.
source_refs.author: Qingyue Zhao, Kaixuan Ji, Heyang Zhao, Tong Zhang, Quanquan Gu

source_refs.claim: The tabular analysis exhibits a large separation between D2-type and pointwise coverage, but does not characterize the joint feasible set under low-dimensional linear reward structure.
source_refs.author: Kaixuan Ji, Qiwei Di, Heyang Zhao, Qingyue Zhao, Quanquan Gu

source_refs.claim: The paper shows that offline decision-making limits can require a behavior-policy characterization strictly finer than previously used scalar coverage notions.
source_refs.author: Thanh Nguyen-Tang, Raman Arora

open_problems.why_unsolved: The known incomparability statement is for a broad function-class D2 quantity, while the tabular extremal relation uses coordinate indicators that eliminate feature sharing. In a d-dimensional linear class, the same theta simultaneously determines rewards, Gibbs likelihood ratios, and the target covariance, so arbitrary choices of C and D need not be realizable. Without a feasibility theorem, lower bounds indexed by only one coefficient may compare different instance shells rather than identify which coverage quantity controls risk.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient characterization of realizable (C,D) pairs for bounded linear Gibbs models, together with a risk-equivalence theorem or explicit counterexample family deciding whether fixed-D shells with different C have the same minimax complexity.

writing_exemplar.why: Its coverage section introduces both coefficients side by side, explains their statistical meanings, and explicitly isolates their incomparability.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: offline learning is governed by data coverage -> reverse-KL analysis exposes pointwise and function-space notions -> broad classes make them incomparable -> characterize their joint geometry after imposing linear Gibbs structure

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt policy-transfer coefficients and matching minimax arguments that characterize behavior-policy quality relative to a function class rather than through uniform density ratios.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result likewise requires an exact function-class-aware characterization and then a theorem relating it to minimax risk.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt information-theoretic lower bounds and attaining algorithms expressed through linear-design geometry for passive contextual best-policy identification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its covariance/design formulation is a close analogue for deriving realizability constraints and hardness from shared linear features rather than independent tabular coordinates.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one construct a same-exact-shell information-theoretic packing of linear Gibbs-reward instances that holds both C and D fixed and proves a lower bound of order d D min{eta/epsilon, epsilon^-2}, rather than a lower bound over an inequality class such as C(pi*) at most C0?

source_refs.claim: The lower bound controls pointwise coverage through an upper-bounded instance class; it does not preserve an exact feature-coverage shell.
source_refs.author: Qingyue Zhao, Kaixuan Ji, Heyang Zhao, Tong Zhang, Quanquan Gu

source_refs.claim: The paper reports that ordinary Le Cam, Assouad, and Fano arguments are not sharp in its slow regime with multiple optima, and introduces a tabular pairing-and-counting construction.
source_refs.author: Kaixuan Ji, Qiwei Di, Heyang Zhao, Qingyue Zhao, Quanquan Gu

source_refs.claim: The paper develops an interactive Fano framework because classical packing methods can miss decision-making hardness and need complexity-aware constructions.
source_refs.author: Fan Chen, Dylan J. Foster, Yanjun Han, Jian Qian, Alexander Rakhlin, Yunbei Xu

open_problems.why_unsolved: Changing a linear reward perturbation changes pi* through the softmax/Gibbs map and therefore moves both the density ratio C and the target covariance defining D. The existing reverse-KL lower bound only controls C by an upper inequality, while the tabular phase-transition proof uses independent arm coordinates and a multiple-optima counting argument. Standard hypercube perturbations therefore leak across shells or lose the factor dD, especially in the weak-regularization regime.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit finite packing indexed by d-dimensional sign or subspace perturbations, with exact-shell calibration of C and D, pairwise observation-KL control, and a Fano/Assouad or pairing-counting theorem yielding the claimed lower bound in both regularization regimes.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates the lower-bound obstruction through the failure of standard methods in the slow regime and makes the new combinatorial device a central contribution.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: reverse-KL creates two statistical regimes -> ordinary two-point and hypercube bounds miss slow-regime hardness -> tabular pairing-and-counting restores sharpness -> construct a feature-shared analogue that remains on one exact (C,D) shell

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over measure tilting plus pairing-and-counting over instances with many optimal arms, separately calibrated for the fast and slow regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest construction already producing the desired reverse-KL phase transition, though it must be redesigned to preserve feature covariance.

method_exemplars.technique: Use complexity-aware Fano reductions and fractional coverings that combine estimation packing with decision loss.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The exact-shell task also needs a packing whose statistical indistinguishability and downstream decision loss are controlled simultaneously under structural constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt change-of-measure lower bounds for passive contextual linear policy identification expressed through feature-design information matrices.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the linear covariance calibration needed to replace independent tabular arms with shared-feature alternatives while retaining an explicit information bound.

open_problems.open_problem: Is there a polynomial-time, data-driven localized-pessimistic Gibbs learner that adapts simultaneously to unknown feature coverage D and the fast/slow regularization regime while attaining the exact-shell minimax rate?

source_refs.claim: KL-PCB obtains a fast rate with a pointwise function-class divergence bonus and a pessimistic reward estimator, but its theorem does not establish exact-shell adaptivity across the weak-regularization regime.
source_refs.author: Qingyue Zhao, Kaixuan Ji, Heyang Zhao, Tong Zhang, Quanquan Gu

source_refs.claim: PUNC is adaptively minimax over multiple norm-constrained offline linear-bandit classes, showing that covariance-aware adaptation is possible without reverse-KL regularization.
source_refs.author: Gene Li, Cong Ma, Nathan Srebro

source_refs.claim: The paper gives an oracle-efficient reduction for pessimistic offline policy optimization, but not the reverse-KL curvature rate or a two-coverage exact-shell guarantee.
source_refs.author: Lequn Wang, Akshay Krishnamurthy, Aleksandrs Slivkins

open_problems.why_unsolved: The reverse-KL fast-rate proof needs a one-sided pessimistic error compatible with the Gibbs map, while the slow regime needs variance-scale rather than curvature-scale localization. Existing linear algorithms show adaptivity for unregularized norm-constrained classes, and generic oracle-efficient pessimism shows computational tractability, but neither analysis preserves the reverse-KL phase transition or localizes to the target-policy generalized eigenvalue D. A naive worst-direction confidence bonus can pay an all-policy or ambient-condition-number cost.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A specified polynomial-time algorithm based on empirical linear confidence geometry and Gibbs policy optimization, plus a uniform high-probability oracle inequality proving rate adaptation to unknown D and min{eta/epsilon, epsilon^-2} without inputting C or D.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation connects the statistical fast rate directly to a concrete pessimistic Gibbs-policy construction and isolates the covariance argument that an adaptive implementation must preserve.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: reverse-KL curvature promises epsilon^-1 learning -> single-policy coverage requires pessimism -> linear features permit empirical covariance localization -> build a computable learner that adapts to D and automatically switches to the epsilon^-2 regime

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt pessimism via an infinity-norm confidence set in whitened linear coordinates, with simultaneous minimax guarantees over unknown norm-constrained instance classes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest established template for coverage-adaptive, computable pessimism under shared linear features.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer its reduction of pessimistic offline policy optimization to supervised-learning oracles while retaining statistical guarantees.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the computational reduction needed to turn a localized pessimistic objective into an implementable procedure.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt lower-confidence-bound learning that is minimax across an unknown continuum of offline-data compositions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its proof architecture demonstrates how one pessimistic learner can adapt to unknown coverage without tuning to the shell parameter.

open_problems.open_problem: When the logging policy mu differs from the reverse-KL reference policy pi_ref, what is the minimax sample complexity for offline linear Gibbs-policy learning in terms of feature covariance under mu and the distinct density-ratio shifts from mu to pi* and pi_ref?

source_refs.claim: The setup assumes for simplicity that the known KL reference policy is also the behavior policy generating the offline data.
source_refs.author: Qingyue Zhao, Kaixuan Ji, Heyang Zhao, Tong Zhang, Quanquan Gu

source_refs.claim: The tabular exact-rate analysis likewise identifies pi_ref with the data-generating behavior policy.
source_refs.author: Kaixuan Ji, Qiwei Di, Heyang Zhao, Qingyue Zhao, Quanquan Gu

source_refs.claim: The paper establishes minimax and adaptive contextual-bandit off-policy evaluation when target and behavior policies differ, demonstrating that the logging-to-target shift has its own estimability geometry.
source_refs.author: Yu-Xiang Wang, Alekh Agarwal, Miroslav Dudik

open_problems.why_unsolved: Equating mu and pi_ref collapses two different roles: mu determines observation covariance and statistical information, whereas pi_ref determines the Gibbs optimizer and regularization geometry. Once they differ, coverage of pi* by mu does not alone control how the reference-weighted softmax responds to reward error, and feature covariance under mu can be favorable even when pointwise pi_ref/mu ratios are large. Existing reverse-KL analyses therefore cannot reveal which shift is rate-determining.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp upper-and-lower minimax theorem for mu not equal to pi_ref, expressed through explicit generalized-eigenvalue and density-ratio coefficients, with a reduction showing when the formula collapses to the known mu = pi_ref frontier.

writing_exemplar.why: Its setup cleanly explains behavior regularization and makes the simplifying equality between logging and reference policies explicit, providing the natural narrative pivot.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: reverse KL anchors the learned policy to a reference -> offline samples arrive from a behavior policy -> existing theory identifies these two policies -> separate their geometric and statistical roles and characterize the resulting two-shift frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt minimax analysis and data-driven combination of importance-weighted and model-based estimators under distinct behavior and target policies.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly handles the additional logging-to-target distribution shift that appears when mu and pi_ref no longer coincide.

method_exemplars.technique: Use function-class-aware policy-transfer coefficients with matching offline decision-making upper and lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its transfer geometry is suited to disentangling behavior-policy coverage from the separate reference policy used in the regularized objective.

method_exemplars.technique: Reweight its one-sided pessimistic reward analysis, propagated through the reverse-KL Gibbs map via a covariance monotonicity lemma, from pi_ref-sampled error to mu-sampled error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the core curvature argument that must survive when the reference and sampling measures differ.

literature_map:
1. Zhao, Ji, Zhao, Zhang and Gu (ICLR 2026, arXiv:2502.06051) obtain a reverse-KL fast rate under single-policy coverage, but their upper bound uses D2 feature/function coverage while their lower bound uses pointwise C.
2. The same paper explicitly states that C and D2 cannot generally bound one another, leaving the governing coverage notion unresolved outside special finite/tabular reductions.
3. Ji, Di, Zhao, Zhao and Gu (2026, arXiv:2605.02141) close both eta/epsilon and epsilon^-2 regimes for offline multi-armed bandits and explicitly call linear/general function approximation future work.
4. Ji et al.'s tabular comparison shows a potentially large separation between D2 and C, illustrating why tabular closure does not identify the low-dimensional linear frontier.
5. Li, Ma and Srebro (NeurIPS 2022, arXiv:2205.10671) give covariance-whitened pessimistic learning and adaptive minimaxity for unregularized offline linear contextual bandits.
6. Rashidinejad, Zhu, Ma, Jiao and Russell (NeurIPS 2021, arXiv:2103.12021) show lower-confidence-bound adaptation across unknown offline-data compositions under single-policy concentrability.
7. Nguyen-Tang and Arora (ICML 2024, arXiv:2501.06339) propose policy-transfer coefficients that refine earlier scalar coverage notions for offline decision-making with function approximation.
8. Wang, Krishnamurthy and Slivkins (AISTATS 2024, arXiv:2306.07923) provide oracle-efficient pessimistic offline policy optimization, supplying a computational template but no reverse-KL shell rate.
9. Jiang, Cai and Ma (ICLR 2026 submission, OpenReview 9Ug3gHa9nL) obtain coverage-adaptive minimax rates for nonparametric offline contextual bandits, showing adaptivity in an adjacent model.
10. Vannella, Proutiere, Jedra and Jeong (IEEE INFOCOM 2022, arXiv:2201.02169) derive information-theoretic and attaining sample complexities for passive contextual linear best-policy identification.
11. Chen, Foster, Han, Qian, Rakhlin and Xu (NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2410.05117) develop complexity-aware Fano methods relevant when ordinary Le Cam/Assouad constructions miss decision hardness.
12. Wang, Agarwal and Dudik (ICML 2017, PMLR v70) characterize minimax and adaptive off-policy evaluation with distinct logging and target policies, an analogue for separating behavior from KL reference.
13. Zhao, Ji, Zhao and Gu (2026, arXiv:2605.09214) obtain forward-KL fast and slow rates and reinforce that regularizer direction changes proof geometry; it does not close the reverse-KL linear two-coverage problem.
14. Krishnamurthy, Hadad and Athey (ICML 2021, arXiv:2102.13240) give regression-oracle adaptation to reward-model misspecification, highlighting a robustness axis beyond the exact-realizable shell considered here.
prior_proposal_map:
The current stat_reversekl_two_coverage directory contains only initialization/state artifacts; no prior proposal or reviewer JSON exists for this qid.
The closest accepted bank entry is stat_policy_regret_margin_overlap_v1, which studies offline policy minimax rates under weak coverage and margin structure.
Its Stage 0.5 reviewer attempt 5 prescribes a full-class feasible upper bound with estimated-propensity clipping stability and exact log-factor resolution.
Its archived proposal §11 leaves the lower exponent open outside the calibrated alpha-gamma regime and places adaptation to unknown indices outside scope.
The downgraded stat_neyman_regret_minimax_v1 reviews yield two same-shell frontier analogies: a class-level extremal information program and a constant-sharp matching upper bound.
The offline-policy joint-misspecification v1/v2 reviewer files were also inspected; their strongest gaps concern partial identification under paired sensitivity tubes rather than the present two-coverage minimax-rate target.
A repository-wide scan of proposal, rejected-angle, reviewer, and bank README paths found no prior CausalSmith artifact naming Zhao arXiv:2502.06051, Ji arXiv:2605.02141, or the exact reverse-KL C-D shell.
